### 🎵 Spotify Popularity Predictor {style="color:#1DB954; font-size:1.8em;"}

**Can audio features predict a song's success?**

## The Problem {background-color="#1a1a2e"}

> *Every year, millions of songs are uploaded to Spotify. Most disappear into obscurity. A handful become global hits.*

**The questions record labels, producers and artists all ask:**

::: {.incremental}
- 🎯 **Will this song be a hit?** (Yes / No)
- 📊 **How popular will it score?** (0–100 scale)
:::

<br>

**Our approach:** Use only the **audio properties** of the song — no artist name, no label, no marketing budget.

::: {.muted}
If the sound itself contains enough signal → the model will find it.
:::

---

## The Data {background-color="#1a1a2e"}

**Spotify Tracks Dataset** — Maharshi Pandya, Kaggle 2022

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Scale**

- 📦 ~114,000 tracks
- 🎸 114 music genres
- 📐 21 features per track
- 📅 Diverse release years
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Audio features measured**

| Feature | Meaning |
|---------|---------|
| danceability | How suitable for dancing |
| energy | Intensity and activity |
| loudness | Overall dB level |
| valence | Musical positiveness |
| tempo | Beats per minute |
| acousticness | Acoustic vs electronic |
| instrumentalness | Vocals present? |
| + 8 more | ... |
:::

:::

::: {.muted}
Target variable: **popularity** (0–100) — Spotify calculates this from recent play counts
:::

---

## Our Approach {background-color="#1a1a2e"}

**Two ML tasks, trained in parallel:**

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}
### 🔵 Classification
*Will this song be popular?*

- Target: popularity **≥ 70** → Popular (1)
- Target: popularity **< 70** → Not popular (0)
- Metrics: F1, ROC-AUC
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
### 🟢 Regression
*What exact score will it get?*

- Target: raw popularity score
- Range: 0 to 100
- Metrics: R², RMSE, MAE
:::

:::

<br>

**Model ladder** — trained in this order:

```
Dummy baseline  →  Linear model  →  Decision Tree  →  XGBoost + CV tuning
```

All models use `random_state=42`. Preprocessing inside scikit-learn `Pipeline` — **no data leakage**.

---

## Key EDA Findings {background-color="#1a1a2e"}

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}
**Finding 1 — Severe class imbalance**

Only **5.1%** of songs reach popularity ≥ 70

- 5,465 popular songs
- 101,442 not popular songs
- → Accuracy alone is misleading (a model that always says "no" scores 95%!)
- → We use **F1** and **ROC-AUC** instead

**Finding 2 — Popularity clusters near 0 and 20–40**

Most songs score very low. The distribution is right-skewed with a large spike at 0 (obscure tracks).
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
**Finding 3 — Weak individual correlations**

No single feature strongly predicts popularity. The best correlations:

| Feature | r with popularity |
|---------|:-----------------:|
| loudness | +0.13 |
| energy | +0.09 |
| acousticness | −0.10 |
| instrumentalness | −0.12 |

**Finding 4 — Genre matters**

Pop, dance, and hip-hop genres score consistently higher than classical, ambient, or sleep music.
:::

:::

::: {.muted}
Conclusion: popularity prediction requires combining many weak signals — exactly what XGBoost is designed for.
:::

---

## Model Results {background-color="#1a1a2e"}

**Classification leaderboard** (test set, n = 21,382)

| Model | F1 | ROC-AUC | Notes |
|-------|:--:|:-------:|-------|
| DummyClassifier | 0.000 | 0.500 | Always predicts "not popular" |
| Logistic Regression | 0.147 | 0.712 | Linear boundary, limited |
| Decision Tree (depth=6) | 0.152 | 0.722 | Slight overfit on train |
| **XGBoost** | **0.437** | **0.920** | Best — gradient boosting |

<br>

**Regression leaderboard** (test set, n = 21,382)

| Model | R² | MAE | RMSE |
|-------|----|-----|------|
| DummyRegressor | 0.000 | 17.8 | 21.2 |
| Ridge Regression | 0.045 | 17.0 | 20.8 |
| Decision Tree (depth=6) | 0.092 | 16.2 | 20.2 |
| **XGBoost** | **0.380** | **12.2** | **16.7** |

::: {.muted}
All metrics on held-out test set — never seen during training or tuning.
:::

---

## What the Model Learned {background-color="#1a1a2e"}

**Most influential audio features (from XGBoost feature importance):**

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Positive drivers of popularity**

- 🎵 **Genre** — pop, dance, hip-hop score higher
- 🔊 **Loudness** — louder (closer to 0 dB) = more popular
- 💃 **Danceability** — high danceability correlates with hits
- ⚡ **Energy** — energetic tracks perform better
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Negative drivers of popularity**

- 🎹 **Instrumentalness** — more vocals = more popular
- 🎸 **Acousticness** — electronic sounds outperform acoustic
- 😴 **Duration** — very long tracks score lower
- 🎙 **Speechiness** — too many words hurts (podcasts, spoken word)
:::

:::

<br>

**Engineered features** that helped: `dance × energy` interaction, `energy / acousticness` ratio

::: {.muted}
These combinations capture "club music" and "produced sound" signals that no single feature can.
:::

## Honest Evaluation {background-color="#1a1a2e"}

### What the model does well ✅

- **Ranks** popular vs unpopular reliably (ROC-AUC 0.92)
- **Finds 76%** of genuinely popular songs (recall)
- **Narrows the field** — useful as a first filter in large catalogs
- Learns that genre, energy, and danceability matter more than tempo or key

### What the model cannot do ❌

- **Predict viral hits** — timing, social media, cultural moments are invisible to audio features
- **Evaluate artistic merit** — it rewards commercial conventions, not originality
- **Work for niche genres** — small sample sizes reduce reliability
- **Replace human judgment** — a model trained on the past cannot anticipate tomorrow's trends

### The honest number

> **R² = 0.38** — audio features explain only **38%** of popularity variance.
> The remaining **62%** is driven by artist fame, marketing, and everything outside the sound.

---

## Conclusions & Recommendations {background-color="#191414"}

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
### For artists & producers

- Prioritise **genre fit** — choose a commercial genre intentionally
- Aim for **high energy + high danceability** for mainstream appeal
- Keep tracks **under 4 minutes**
- Make tracks **loud** (within streaming standards)

*These are patterns — not rules. Originality still matters.*
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### For labels & platforms

- Use the model as a **first-pass filter** on demo submissions
- Apply it to **cold-start** recommendations for newly uploaded tracks (no plays yet)
- Do **not** use it as the final gatekeeper — human expertise remains essential

:::

:::

<br>

::: {style="text-align: center; padding: 1em; background: #1a1a2e; border-radius: 8px;"}
**Key takeaway:** Popularity is about 38% sound and 62% everything else.
Audio features are a useful signal — not the whole story.
